member.summary: Sends a to this connection.
member.param: A token (integer number), formatted as string and "encrypted" with the 3-byte XOR key (FC CF AB).
member.remarks: Is sent by the client when: This packet is sent by the client after it connected to the server, to authenticate itself. Causes reaction on server side: The server will check the token. If it's correct, the client gets added to the requested chat room.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.Network.Packets.ChatServer.ConnectionExtensions.SendChatRoomClientJoinedAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.Network.IConnection,System.Byte,System.String)
member.summary: Sends a to this connection.
member.remarks: Is sent by the server when: This packet is sent by the server after another chat client joined the chat room. Causes reaction on client side: The client will add the client in its list (if over 2 clients are connected to the same room), or show its name in the title bar.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.Network.Packets.ChatServer.ConnectionExtensions.SendLeaveChatRoomAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.Network.IConnection)
member.summary: Sends a to this connection.
member.remarks: Is sent by the client when: This packet is sent by the client when it leaves the chat room, before the connection closes. Causes reaction on server side: The server will remove the client from the chat room, notifying the remaining clients.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.Network.Packets.ChatServer.ConnectionExtensions.SendChatRoomClientLeftAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.Network.IConnection,System.Byte,System.String)
member.summary: Sends a to this connection.
member.remarks: Is sent by the server when: This packet is sent by the server after a chat client left the chat room. Causes reaction on client side: The client will remove the client from its list, or mark its name in the title bar as offline.

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.Network.Packets.ClientToServer.QuestSelectRequest
member.summary: Is sent by the client when: The client opened an quest NPC dialog and selected an available quests. Causes reaction on server side: If the quest is already active, it responds with the QuestProgress. If the quest is inactive, the server decides if the character can start the quest and responds with a QuestStepInfo with the StartingNumber. A character can run up to 3 concurrent quests at a time.

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.Network.Packets.ClientToServer.QuestProceedRequest
member.summary: Is sent by the client when: After the server started a quest (and sent a F60B message) the game client requests to proceed with the quest. Causes reaction on server side: The quest state is set accordingly on the server. The next response seems to depend on the quest configuration. Depending on the action of the next quest state, the server will send either a quest progress message (F60C) or again a quest start message (F60B).

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.Network.Packets.ClientToServer.QuestCompletionRequest
member.summary: Is sent by the client when: The game client requests to complete an active quest. Causes reaction on server side: The server checks the conditions to complete the quest. If this fails, nothing happens. If all conditions are met, the reward is given to the player and the quest state is set accordingly, so that the player can select to start the next quest. Additionally, the quest completion response message (F60D) is sent to the client.

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.Network.Packets.ClientToServer.NpcBuffRequest
member.summary: Is sent by the client when: The game client requests to get a buff from the currently interacting quest npc. As far as we know, only the Elf Soldier NPC offers such a buff until a certain character level (150 or 220). Causes reaction on server side: The server should check if the correct Quest NPC (e.g. Elf Soldier) dialog is opened and the player didn't reach the level limit yet. If that's both the case, it adds a defined buff (MagicEffect) to the player; Otherwise, a message is sent to the player.

member.summary: Is sent by the client when: After the server started a quest (and sent a F60B message) the game client requests to proceed with the quest. member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.Network.Packets.ClientToServer.QuestClientActionRequestRef
member.summary: Is sent by the client when: The game client requests to complete a client action, e.g. completing a tutorial. member.summary: Sends a to this connection.
member.param: The name of the character which should be deleted.

A security code (7 bytes long). Some game clients/servers also expect to transmit the account password (up to 20 bytes long) here. In OpenMU, we work with the security here, but are not limiting to a length of 7 bytes.
member.remarks: Is sent by the client when: The game client is at the character selection screen and the player requests to delete an existing character. Causes reaction on server side: The server checks if the player transmitted the correct security code and if the character actually exists. If all is valid, it deletes the character from the account. It then sends a response with a result code back to the game client.

Depending on the action of the next quest state, the server will send either a quest progress message (F60C) or again a quest start message (F60B).

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.Network.Packets.ClientToServer.ConnectionExtensions.SendQuestCompletionRequestAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.Network.IConnection,System.UInt16,System.UInt16)
member.summary: Sends a to this connection.
member.remarks: Is sent by the client when: The game client requests to complete an active quest. Causes reaction on server side: The server checks the conditions to complete the quest. If this fails, nothing happens. If all conditions are met, the reward is given to the player and the quest state is set accordingly, so that the player can select to start the next quest. Additionally, the quest completion response message (F60D) is sent to the client.

member.remarks: Is sent by the client when: The game client requests to cancel an active quest. Causes reaction on server side: The server checks if the quest is currently in progress. In this case, the quest state is reset and a response (F60F) is sent back to the client.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.Network.Packets.ClientToServer.ConnectionExtensions.SendQuestClientActionRequestAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.Network.IConnection,System.UInt16,System.UInt16)
member.summary: Sends a to this connection.
member.remarks: Is sent by the client when: The game client requests to complete a client action, e.g. completing a tutorial. Causes reaction on server side: The server checks if the specified quest is currently in progress. If the quest got a Condition (condition type 0x10) for this flag, the condition is flagged as fulfilled.

member.summary: Sends a to this connection.
member.remarks: Is sent by the client when: The game client requests to get a buff from the currently interacting quest npc. As far as we know, only the Elf Soldier NPC offers such a buff until a certain character level (150 or 220). member.summary: Sends a to this connection.
member.param: Detail state; semantics depend on the main State field. See the game logic enums for per-state values.
1 = entrance is open (Enter button enabled); 0 = entrance closed.
Number of players currently inside the event map (capped at 255).
Remaining time in seconds. Standby: seconds until event opens. Tower: seconds the tower has been open. Otherwise 0.
member.remarks: Is sent by the server when: The player requests state information from the Kanturu gateway NPC. Causes reaction on client side: The client shows the Kanturu entry dialog (INTERFACE_KANTURU2ND_ENTERNPC) with event state, detail state, whether entry is possible, current player count and remaining time.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.Network.Packets.ServerToClient.ConnectionExtensions.SendKanturuStateChangeAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.Network.IConnection,MUnique.OpenMU.Network.Packets.ServerToClient.KanturuStateChange.StateType,System.Byte)
member.summary: Sends a to this connection.
member.param: Refers to the KanturuStateInfo.StateType enum values.

Detail state within the main state. Maya battle: 0=none, 2=notify, 3=monster1, 4=maya1, 8=monster2, 9=maya2, 13=monster3, 14=maya3, 16=endcycle. Nightmare: 0=none, 1=idle, 2=intro, 3=battle, 4=end. Tower: 0=none, 1=revitalization, 2=notify, 3=close.
member.remarks: Is sent by the server when: The Kanturu event transitions to a new phase or sub-phase. Causes reaction on client side: The client shows or hides the in-map HUD, switches background music, and when entering the Tower state reloads the barrier-open terrain file (EncTerrain_n_01.att) to visually remove the Elphis barrier.
